newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to plant record soybean crop in 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to plant record soybean crop in 1997/98.

text.p: Brazil's soybean crop should reach a record 29.33 million tonnes in 1997/98, with planted area forecast to rise eight percent to 12.35 million hectares, independent consultant Safras e Mercado said.
"There is no doubt that this (acreage) is a substantial figure and it should result in a record crop next harvest," said analyst Flavio Franca.
The figures were the first forecasts by Safras for the 1997/98 planting and crop.
Franca said the soybean harvest should rise to 29.33 million tonnes, up 13 percent on this year's 26.02 million tonnes, based on average yields, a favourable climate and investments in technology.
"There is no shortage of reasons for producers to be optimistic," he said.
Prices were 35 percent above the 10-year average in 1996/97 due to low world stocks and high prices on the Chicago commodities futures exchange, he noted.
Planting would also be boosted by the abolition of an export tax on soybeans and soy products which has fuelled export sales to record levels in 1997, he said.

Other positive factors were a reduction in growers' debts, the ample supply of inputs, new export corridors and a package of government incentives, including higher financing limits and lower interest rates.
The key growing state of Parana was set to produce 7.31 million tonnes in 1997/98, with planted area seen up eight percent at 2.76 million hectares.

In Rio Grande do Sul, production was forecast to rise to 6.14 million tonnes with a planted area of 3.07 million hectares, up four percent on the previous year. Mato Grosso was due to produce 5.9 million tonnes from planted area of 2.27 million hectares, up 10 percent.
